question: Can knowledge whose nature is object-illumination shine by its own nature if it is unmanifest?
premises: Knowledge is taken as having the illumination of objects as its nature.
If that knowledge is unmanifest, it does not appear.
Even its inherent self does not shine by its own nature.
inference: Knowledge cannot ground manifestation if it is itself unmanifest and not self-luminous.
uncertainties: The truncated form samavāyy is read as samavāyin/samavāyī in sandhi; analysis follows that reading.
plain_english: Knowledge is of the nature of illuminating objects, yet if it is unmanifest, even its inherent self does not shine by its own nature.
